answer: Rate-limit identity creation and tie each new identity to a proof of unique personhood, checked against a liveness atlas of verified humans. One person may register only a few agent identities per epoch, so a sybil farm cannot ripple outward into thousands of fake workers. Each proof is bound to a single opal-like unique token that cannot be duplicated or resold, and every extra identity costs a fresh, time-consuming verification. An attacker wanting a thousand fake agents must pass a thousand separate personhood checks, making the attack slow, expensive, and easy to spot.
